access_control.analysis: IP allowlist / geofence. Access restricted to specific source IPs (likely Saudi Arabia or internal networks).

findings.title: IP Allowlist / Geofence Restriction (Confirmed)
findings.impact: Confirms WAF/CDN presence with IP allowlisting. Active scanning must be done from an authorized Saudi IP.

findings.title: Wildcard TLS Certificate in Use
findings.detection_logic: TLS handshake reveals CN=*.chi.gov.sa wildcard certificate
findings.impact: Wildcard cert means any subdomain takeover under *.chi.gov.sa would leverage this cert. Enumerate all subdomains.

findings.title: Short-lived Certificate (30-day validity)
findings.impact: 30-day certs suggest automated renewal (Let's Encrypt or ACME). Check for .well-known/acme-challenge exposure.
reproduction: echo | openssl s_client -connect greeting.chi.gov.sa:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

owasp_top10_checklist.manual_check: Test for stored/reflected XSS in greeting message text
owasp_top10_checklist.note: High-value target for a greeting service

owasp_top10_checklist.manual_check: Test IDOR by enumerating greeting IDs (sequential or UUIDs)
owasp_top10_checklist.note: Greeting services often expose other users' private greetings

owasp_top10_checklist.manual_check: Check for missing CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options
owasp_top10_checklist.note: Cannot verify until access from Saudi IP

owasp_top10_checklist.manual_check: Check if greeting share links use predictable/short tokens
owasp_top10_checklist.note: Short tokens = enumerable; check token entropy

owasp_top10_checklist.manual_check: Check for rate limiting on login, password reset, OTP flows
owasp_top10_checklist.note: Saudi government portals often use Absher/national ID login

recommendations: Run active scan from Saudi IP (KSA VPN or Termux on Saudi mobile network)
Test ACME challenge path: /.well-known/acme-challenge/ (due to 30-day cert)
Use nuclei with header/misconfiguration templates once access is established
